title: Don’t Feature Branch | Dave Farley’s Weblog
summary: Dave Farley argues feature branches are either not isolated (so not branches) or incompatible with CI; commenters defend branch-per-feature and attack feature toggles.

assertions.quote: the merge problem it faces could be nothing at all or represent days or even weeks of effort
No merge tool can predict that the features that I write and features that you write will work nicely together

verdicts.note: Semantic conflicts are invisible to textual merge; this is the standard rationale for CI.

assertions.quote: if you decide to merge only one of them back to head, you are about to release a previously untested scenario

verdicts.note: Logically sound; the size of the risk depends on how coupled the features are.

assertions.quote: Trunk Based Development with Feature toggles are simpler for a team to use and implement than feature branches

verdicts.note: Survey data favours trunk-based teams, but 'simpler' is a judgment and toggles carry their own cost.

DORA finds trunk-based development with frequent check-in predicts delivery performance, but it does not compare it with disciplined branch-per-feature or measure simplicity, and does not study feature toggles.

assertions.quote: You set yourself up for disappointment when you want to release and can’t take out a feature.

verdicts.note: True without toggles; feature flags give trunk-based teams the same ability at some complexity cost.

assertions.quote: I find them the biggest hack of what’s in ci these days and a potential source of errors

verdicts.note: Toggle debt and misconfiguration incidents are real, but branches trade them for merge risk; no comparison exists.
